thread:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] service:inference - latency_surge detected (p99 > 1200ms) in us-west-2 hosted tier. paging on-call. details: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/3012345678 :rotating_light:

oncall_ee: on it, looking at p95/p99. grabbing traces now.

oncall_ee: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1350ms across text-gen endpoints. streaming sessions show stalls (~2-4s stall windows) intermittently.

samira: noticed sudden increase in mixed sequence length requests at 15:12UTC, upstream traffic spike ~3x for short+long combos. could be mixed-seq amplification.

jordan: can we narrow to deployment? is this on the dedicated pools or hosted autoscale nodes?

oncall_ee: graphs show most errors and latency from the continuous-batching path on hosted GPU pools (pool-id usw2-hosted-gpu-3). Dedicated looks fine.

mike-sre: thanks. any recent rollout that touches batching scheduler or kv cache?

oncall_ee: no deployments in last 2 hrs. config changes: autoscaler had a short glitch at 15:10 but recovered. suspect scheduling fairness + mixed seq lengths causing large batch padding + long tail.

lia: streaming traces show repeated preemption attempts for streaming workers — streaming requests getting shoved to low priority and then waiting for large batch formation.

samira: this matches: long requests waiting for small short requests to coalesce into a full batch => padding blowup and tail waits. Also KV cache eviction spikes noted.

product-ed: any customer impact? SLA pages?

oncall_ee: no broad error increase, mostly latency. We have 3 high-traffic customers reporting slow interactive experiences (chat UI lagging). I'll open empathy notes.

ops-bot: correlate: rolling restart event for model-compiler-manager at 15:11 triggered by OOM recovery on node-42. Impact: ~12% capacity transiently.

mike-sre: capacity dip + mixed sequence mix is classic for batch-size amplification. Plan: 1) short-term mitigation route streaming & interactive traffic to high-priority fast-path (bypass continuous batcher) 2) throttle lower-priority background batchers 3) adjust max_batch_delay from 12ms -> 6ms on affected pool.

jordan: can we quickly apply routing rule? I can push a policy to route requests with header X-Client-Type:interactive to the low-latency queue. Needs a quick config jump.

oncall_ee: do it. add canary for 10% traffic first.

jordan: pushing rule now -> runbook command: `rbctl route add --pool usw2-hosted-gpu-3 --match 'header:X-Client-Type==interactive' --target lowlatency-queue --weight 10`

samira: monitoring dashboards: /dash/contbatch/usw2/latency - watching p99.

ops-bot: routing rule applied (10% canary).

oncall_ee: canary looks promising: p99 for routed subset ~480ms down from 1350ms. overall p99 down to ~980ms. continue rollout.

mike-sre: proceed to 50% if stable for 2 minutes.

jordan: bumping to 50% now. `rbctl route update --name interactive-canary --weight 50`

lia: also lowering max_batch_delay to 6ms on pool. `infractl set scheduler --pool usw2-hosted-gpu-3 --max-batch-delay-ms 6`

ops-bot: scheduler param applied on 6/8 nodes. one node retrying.

oncall_ee: after metrics: overall p95 down to 300ms, p99 down to 560ms 3min after change. streaming stall windows much shorter.

product-ed: any regression risk from lowering max_batch_delay? more compute spend?

mike-sre: small increase in per-token cost due to less batching efficiency, but acceptable short-term. We'll revert once queued mix stabilizes.

samira: next steps for medium-term: tune batch size caps to prevent gigantic padding when long+short mixes, and implement preemptive fairness (limit how long a long request can block batch flush). Also KV cache tuning to avoid eviction storms during capacity dips.

oncall_ee: opening a ticket for follow-up fixes: INC-3012346 - Batching fairness + seqlen amplification. Assign to eng-runtime.

lia: I recommend adding a fallback: if p99 > 800ms for > 5m, auto-route interactive to lowlatency-queue at 30% and lower max_batch_delay automatically.

jordan: we can prototype a temporary rule in the routing controller. I'll coordinate with runtime.

ops-bot: Customer outreach: flagged customers A, B, C with support tickets #4532 #4533 #4534. Sent initial status update.

oncall_ee: handoff in 30m to next on-call: samira will lead follow-ups and postmortem.

samira: taking over. doc pointer: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/3012345678 - I'll add timeline and mitigation steps.

mike-sre: follow-ups: (1) root-cause investigation of compiler-manager OOM event and capacity ripple (2) add preemptive batch flush after X ms or Y short-request count (3) KV eviction backpressure on scheduler.

product-ed: please keep comms team updated for any customer-facing messaging.

oncall_ee: closing incident page for now; monitoring for 1 hour. If p99 creeps up again we'll re-open pager. Great work all :thumbsup:

samira: noted. I'll run an eval with mixed-seqlen traffic to reproduce and validate fixes in staging. Will post reproducer and suggested config changes in the ticket.

ops-bot: incident closed (mitigated) by oncall_ee. duration ~ 00:22:00.

mike-sre: postmortem owner: samira. ETA initial draft 48h.

product-ed: flagged potential SLA note for enterprise customers affected; we'll prepare short blurb.

samira: posting debug snippets in the ticket: sample trace with stall: ```
TRACE id=abc123 pool=usw2-hosted-gpu-3 seqlens=[12,512] wait_before_flush=18ms batch_size=64
worker logs: preempt_attempt=1 preempt_wait=120ms flush_trigger=pad_threshold
```

samira: also attaching query histograms and canary rollout logs.

oncall_ee: thanks team. handing off - out.

(threads ends)
